messages:
nina: quick sync — need a decision on embeddings cache for MVP. Ops says it will save tokens/cost for common queries, but infra effort is non-trivial.

hudson: short take: a read-only cache (serve cached vectors for exact-key hits) is cheap to add (~3d infra + 2d QA). full writeback + precompute pipeline is a bigger lift (~3w).

priya: product POV: early pilots care about latency and cost predictability. caching reduces both. but we should avoid promising full freshness guarantees in MVP.

rachel: support risk: cache invalidation edge cases cause stale results reports. if we ship read-only, add clear messaging and an expunge endpoint for support to use.

evan: performance numbers: our small pilot logs show 18% of embedding requests are duplicates. caching those could cut embedding cost ~15% and reduce 90th pct latency by ~60ms.

hudson: suggestion: MVP scope = read-through cache with TTL + manual invalidation endpoint. v1 scope = async writeback, precompute jobs, and consistency hooks.

priya: sounds reasonable. add launch gate: metrics threshold for cache hit rate and a rollback plan if error rate > 1%.

rachel: i'll draft the support playbook (how to evict, how to validate) and sample incident runbook.

hudson: i'll add infra tasks: cache layer (Redis tier), feature-flag, TTL 5m default, manual expunge endpoint. QA will add regression tests for staleness windows.

evan: i'll instrument a quick sampling job to validate hit rate during canary.

nina: decision: include read-through embeddings cache in MVP with TTL+manual eviction, defer writeback/precompute to v1. Milestones: MVP ship week +2w; v1 GA target +8w.

priya: i'll update the PRD and customer comms to set expectations (no freshness SLAs for MVP).

hudson: tasks assigned and feature-flagged.

rachel: support playbook ETA 48h.

calendar-bot: "Event created: Embeddings cache MVP check-in Friday 09:30"

nina: resolving this thread. reopen if someone thinks we need full writeback for pilot customers. :white_check_mark:
